**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected plant part**: Sugarcane leaf (cross-section/close-up of leaf blade)
- **Key features observed**:
  - Distinct **longitudinal yellow-green streaking** running parallel to the leaf veins
  - Alternating bands of yellow/golden, light green, and darker green running the length of the leaf
  - Yellow-orange discoloration at the margins fading to lighter green/white in the central zone
  - A few small reddish-brown spots visible on the surface
  - The streaking pattern is oriented along the leaf axis, not as irregular patches

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Brown_Spot**: Ruled out — no discrete brown oval/circular spots matching this disease
- **Grassy_Shoot**: Ruled out — this is a leaf section, not abnormal shoot proliferation
- **Leaf_Scald**: Possible but less likely — Leaf Scald shows cream/white scalded lesions with a pencil-line border, not this striped pattern
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Shows irregular mosaic patches (light/dark green intermingled) — the pattern here is more streaked than mottled
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Strong match — SCSMV causes **distinct yellow and green longitudinal streaks** running parallel to the veins, exactly matching the alternating banded coloration seen here
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Ruled out — Yellow Leaf shows midrib yellowing from tip, not longitudinal streaking
- **Yellow_Spot**: Ruled out — no discrete yellow spots

The longitudinal alternating yellow/green streaks running parallel to leaf veins is the hallmark symptom of Sugarcane Streak Mosaic Virus (SCSMV).
